title: bug: chat_decision posts into a channel without chat_send's sender and channel checks: it accepts workerId "system" (posts as the daemon) or an unregistered id (resets a paused loop guard), and reports success while posting nothing for "#general" or an unknown channel
description:
Filed by defect hunt 11-03 #3 (task-859eff80). It is a family gap: moe.chat_decision puts a chat message into a channel, but skips the checks its sibling moe.chat_send applies to exactly that post.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatDecision.ts:30-34 passes `proposedBy: params.workerId || 'unknown'` and the raw `channel` straight to state.createDecision. Neither value is checked.
- createDecision (state/chatStore.ts:591-631):
  - caps content by CHARACTERS (sanitizeString 10240, :598);
  - writes the decision file and the map entry (:613-617);
  - only then posts, and only when the channel is an exact id (`state.channels.has(opts.channel)`, :620), with `sender: opts.proposedBy` (:621-626).
- The sibling, tools/chatSend.ts:
  - :34-52 refuse sender "system" with NOT_ALLOWED. Its comment: accepting it "would let any /mcp agent impersonate the daemon and reset the mentionRouter loop-guard". They also refuse a sender that is not a registered worker ("Unknown sender").
  - :55-56 resolve the channel with resolveChannelRef (id, name or "#name") and refuse an unknown one with NOT_FOUND.
  - resolveChannelRef's docstring (chatStore.ts:88-100) says: "Every chat tool that takes a channel from a caller goes through this".
- MentionRouter (util/mentionRouter.ts:212-235):
  - routes sender "system" as daemon bookkeeping;
  - treats any sender that is not a known worker as HUMAN, which resets the hop count and clears a loop-guard pause (:226-235).

CONSEQUENCES
- A caller can post "[Decision Proposed] …" as "system", impersonating the daemon. chat_send refuses this.
- A caller can post as an unregistered id. That includes the default 'unknown' when no workerId is given, or a seat purged by a daemon restart. The post silently un-pauses a channel the loop guard stopped.
- `channel: "#general"`, the form chat_send and the role docs use, returns success:true with messageId null and posts nothing. So a human watching #general never sees the proposal. An unknown channel id also returns success.
- Multi-byte content inside the character cap but over the 10KB BYTE cap of sendMessage (chatStore.ts:190-191) throws "Message content exceeds 10KB limit" AFTER the decision is persisted. Each retry leaves another orphan decision with messageId null.

EVIDENCE
- Repro on HEAD ef5c7101. A hunt subagent wrote it in /tmp/hunt-859e-A; I re-ran it myself in /tmp/hunt-859e-snap (git archive with Linux node_modules). Persisted copies: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-859e/A/zzHuntAChatDecision.test.ts and zzHuntAChatDecision.output.txt.
- Command: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/zzHuntAChatDecision.test.ts`. Result: 5 failed of 5.
  - sender "system": chat_send rejects, but chat_decision gives `promise resolved "{ success: true, decision: { …(9) } }" instead of rejecting`.
  - Unregistered sender: chat_send rejects with "Unknown sender". chat_decision posts as worker-ghost after a 5-hop ping-pong paused the channel, and the guard then reads `expected { hopCount: +0, paused: false } to deeply equal { hopCount: 5, paused: true }`.
  - "#general": chat_send posts there. chat_decision gives `expected '#general' to be 'chan-…'`, `expected null not to be null` (messageId) and `expected [ 'via send' ] to include '[Decision Proposed] adopt plan B'`.
  - Unknown channel chan-nope: chat_decision returns success instead of NOT_FOUND.
  - Multi-byte: 4000 '€' (12000 bytes) throws /10KB/, yet getDecisions() already holds the decision.

FIX DIRECTION
- In chatDecision.ts, before any write:
  - apply chat_send's sender rule: refuse "system" with NOT_ALLOWED, and refuse an unregistered id with INVALID_INPUT, using the same disk fallback (state.tryLoadWorkerFromDisk);
  - resolve a given channel with state.resolveChannelRef and refuse an unresolvable one with NOT_FOUND;
  - pass the resolved channel.id to createDecision.
- In createDecision, check the byte size of the "[Decision Proposed] …" line against MAX_CHAT_MESSAGE_BYTES before writing the decision file, so a refused call writes nothing.
- Keep the no-workerId case behaving as today (proposedBy 'unknown'), or refuse it: pick one and state it in the MCP_SERVER.md chat_decision section, with the new refusals and that the channel accepts an id, a name or "#name".
- No other tool changes. The success response shape is unchanged.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatDecision.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/state/chatStore.ts, docs/MCP_SERVER.md (the moe.chat_decision section only, around :2716), plus one NEW test file such as packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatDecision.test.ts. None is held by an open row (lanes.js at 16:23Z).
definitionOfDone: chat_decision refuses workerId "system" (NOT_ALLOWED) and an unregistered workerId (INVALID_INPUT) with chat_send's rules, before any decision file or message is written. A registered seat's decision still posts, and its success response shape is unchanged.

A given channel resolves through resolveChannelRef, so an id, a name or "#name" all post to that channel with messageId set. An unresolvable channel is refused NOT_FOUND. Content over the 10KB byte cap is refused before the decision is persisted, so getDecisions() stays empty.

A NEW test file under packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/ covers the system sender, an unregistered sender (a loop-guard pause must survive the refused call), "#general", an unknown channel and the multi-byte case. Restoring today's chatDecision.ts or createDecision fails it. The docs/MCP_SERVER.md chat_decision section states the new refusals and the accepted channel forms, and `npm run lint` passes at the repo root.
Verification, in a snapshot outside the shared checkout: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/<new test file> src/tools/chatSend.test.ts && npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
